title: Minimal or Mori models for generalized rational lc pairs
exact_target: For every normal integral projective generalized lc rational pair (X,B+M) in characteristic zero, with fixed nef rational b-Cartier data, must there be a projective birational model Y extracting no divisor whose generalized discrepancies do not decrease and increase strictly on contracted X-primes, with nef adjoint if the original adjoint is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a relative-Picard-one Mori contraction to a lower-dimensional normal projective base with relatively antiample adjoint?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For every normal integral projective generalized lc rational pair (X,B+M) in characteristic zero, with fixed nef rational b-Cartier data, must there be a projective birational model Y extracting no divisor whose generalized discrepancies do not decrease and increase strictly on contracted X-primes, with nef adjoint if the original adjoint is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a relative-Picard-one Mori contraction to a lower-dimensional normal projective base with relatively antiample adjoint?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For every normal integral projective generalized lc rational pair (X,B+M) in characteristic zero, with fixed nef rational b-Cartier data, must there be a projective birational model Y extracting no divisor whose generalized discrepancies do not decrease and increase strictly on contracted X-primes, with nef adjoint if the original adjoint is pseudo-effective, and otherwise a relative-Picard-one Mori contraction to a lower-dimensional normal projective base with relatively antiample adjoint?
